title: Apple's New iPhone Lineup Includes First Foldable Model
paragraphs: On September 9, Apple unveiled its latest generation of iPhones, including its first foldable model, the iPhone Duo.
The new lineup was presented by CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1.
The foldable Duo opens to reveal a 7.6-inch screen that is 80% larger than that of the new iPhone 18 Pro. According to Apple, it is the largest display ever offered on an iPhone.

Users can divide the screen between two different apps or open two windows from the same website. This could make it easier to compare products while shopping, for example. The Duo can also be used with an Apple Pencil, which was previously available only for iPads.
However, the new design comes at a high price. Starting at $1,999, the Duo is Apple's most expensive iPhone yet.

Ternus also introduced the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, which start at $1,199 and $1,299. Their prices are about $100 higher than those of the previous generation, partly because of a global shortage of memory chips.
Apple says both models offer significantly better battery life than the previous generation and can charge to 50% in about 15 minutes.

The cameras have also been upgraded. Users can add cinematic effects after recording a video, while a new focus-tracking feature can keep the camera focused on a moving subject, such as a child playing soccer.
The phones also include new AI features for Siri, with Apple hoping its focus on privacy and security will set it apart from rivals that are further ahead with AI.
Preorders for the Pro models begin on September 12, ahead of their release on September 18. Duo preorders begin on October 16, before the phone's release on October 23.
